audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rated every stage "Skill" while the content layer and the packet levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Skill/Malzahar. Five of seven rows disagreed across the two layers, so the page answered "who wins Level 1" two different ways.
audit.why: Malzahar has no dash, no shield beyond Void Shift and no trade tool before 6; Neeko's Tangle-Barbs into Blooming Burst is a real kill pattern from 3. At 6 Nether Grasp suppresses point-blank and Call of the Void silences the combo, which is the genuine even point, and by two-plus items his point-and-click suppress plus Zhonya's outweighs the early lead. 58.62% owner win rate over 203 games supports the early-Neeko reading.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-5 to Neeko, level 6 and first item stay even, two-plus items to Malzahar; every moved row's why rewritten in the same proposal and the ratings moved with it.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why claimed Pop Blossom gives "a 3-second knockup" — a magnitude the kit does not give — and the level 6 spike text did not name Nether Grasp's actual cooldown.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140/110/80 seconds. That number is the whole spike map for this lane: pre-6 is free, 6 is even only while his R is up, and the 80-second rank-3 cooldown is what flips the late game.
audit.corrected: Level 6 why now reads off the 140-second rank-1 cooldown, first item off 110, two-plus items off 80; the invented knockup duration is gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The three decisive interactions were absent from every field. (a) Nether Grasp is a channel, so Tangle-Barbs' root or Pop Blossom's knockup cancels the suppression outright. (b) Void Shift grants crowd-control immunity until he takes damage, so a cold root or a cold Pop Blossom simply does not land. (c) Call of the Void silences on a flat 6-second cooldown, which is what actually loses Neeko her combo.
audit.why: All three come straight from Riot's text plus the per-rank cooldowns in the kit, and two of them are listed in missingInteractions for this exact pairing. Without (b) the reader steps in and wonders why the root did nothing; without (a) they never learn Neeko is one of the cleanest answers to an ult on their carry.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, breakdown.mid, breakdown.late, tradeGood, tradeBad and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all — the catalogued defect 3.
audit.why: The punishable windows here are numeric: Call of the Void is a flat 6 seconds, Malefic Visions 11/10/9/8/7, Nether Grasp 140/110/80.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries 140/110/80 and the flat 6-second silence.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave was champion-generic prose about "lying" that would paste onto any enemy with a name swap.
audit.why: Malefic Visions only spreads when an afflicted unit dies, so denying him minion deaths denies him his clear; a fast crash is a real, enemy-specific wave plan.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around denying Malefic Visions its spread and around his 6-second poke on a frozen wave.

audit.why: Mercurial Scimitar / Quicksilver Sash is one of the few effects that removes suppression, so the existing late-game item advice is sound; breakdown.late now names it instead of describing a flank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed on five bullets: dosFull[0].d carried the suppression warning under a last-hit title, dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string under a clone title, dosFull[2].d was an unrelated claim, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d were a stock line and the tradeBad string.
audit.why: Catalogued defect 2 — the title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: All five bodies rewritten to match their own titles and grounded in Malzahar's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged "His Malefic Visions" as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Malefic Visions is the real name of Malzahar's E in the kit file. Separately, the kit's derived "execute" flag on Malefic Visions misfires: Riot's own text describes the DoT passing to a nearby unit when the target dies, not a health-threshold execute, so no execute claim was written.
audit.corrected: Name left as-is; no execute language added anywhere.

edits.after: Malzahar wins by silencing your combo with Call of the Void, then suppressing you under Nether Grasp before the root lands.

edits.before: Carry through deception — every fight you start disguised begins 5v4 in spirit; your job is the patience the crouch demands.
edits.after: Carry by deleting him: he has no dash, so a landed Tangle-Barbs into triple bloom removes the one champion who can suppress your team.

edits.before: Poke blooms and tell lies — your trades are even and your information war isn't. Every clone he answers wrong is tempo.
edits.after: Trades are not even — he has no dash and no answer before 6, so bloom him off the wave and shove him under his tower.

edits.before: Post-6, hunt clumps: disguise into the wave, R the river contest, root the scatter. One good crouch is a won objective.
edits.after: Post-6 respect his 140-second R: fight when it is spent, and if he ults an ally your root ends the channel instantly.

edits.before: You are the ambush their comp can't draft against: disguise, flank, Pop Blossom on three, root the survivors. The clone scouts the setup for free.
edits.after: Buy Mercurial Scimitar or hold Cleanse — an 80-second Nether Grasp on you is a removed teamfight, and Zhonya's lets him survive your flank.

edits.before: Best wave: a bloom-cleared push that crashes while your clone walks somewhere worth lying about — every shove is also a misdirection. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down and the clone on cooldown — one honest Neeko is half a champion. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: shove into him — Malefic Visions only spreads when an afflicted unit dies, so a fast crash denies him the free clear and pins him under tower. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with Tangle-Barbs down, where his 6-second Call of the Void out-pokes an honest Neeko. Crash timing: crash before 6 and cash it into plates or a roam.

notes: CHART: the full layer had all seven sides as "Skill" while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Skill/Skill/Malzahar. I moved the five disagreeing full-layer rows onto the content values (so no content win[N] edit was needed — the pair is satisfied by bringing full into line) and rewrote each moved row's why plus its rating in the same proposal. DIFF FIELD: diff="EVEN" and diffRating="5.5/10" do not match a 58.62% owner win rate over 203 games, and Malzahar has no pre-6 answer to Tangle-Barbs; this probably wants a favourable token, but I do not know the accepted vocabulary for the diff enum so I left diff, diffRating, carryRating and breakdown.difficulty alone rather than guess a token the renderer may not colour. See questionsForUser. KIT FLAG MISFIRE: the derived "execute" flag on Malefic Visions contradicts Riot's own description (the DoT passes to a nearby unit on death; there is no health threshold), so I wrote no execute language and ignored the execute-threshold missingInteractions headline. The packet's suspectName "His Malefic Visions" is a false positive — that is the real ability name. LEFT ALONE: breakdown.feeding, ahead, loading, tldr, winCon, spikes[0/1/3], early/mid/late content and the whys[] array were already specific to Malzahar and correct; whys[] already matches the corrected chart.
